title: (Technical) feasibility of nano-needle arthroscopy (IONA) in symptomatic total hip arthroplasty – potential for use in the orthopedic outpatient setting: a prospective exploratory clinical feasibility study
summary:
This study investigates a new, particularly minimally invasive method for evaluating pain following implantation of a hip prosthesis. In some cases, these symptoms may be caused by an infection that is difficult to detect.

Currently, a surgical procedure is usually required to establish a definitive diagnosis, either in the form of arthroscopy or open surgical tissue sampling.

In contrast, the new method uses a significantly thinner camera and more delicate instruments (e.g., biopsy forceps) that are inserted directly into the joint. The aim is to enable this procedure to be performed in the outpatient clinic under local anesthesia in the future.

Within the scope of this study, both procedures will be performed consecutively in the same patients during a single surgical session and directly compared.

The objective of the study is to assess whether the new method is technically feasible and capable of providing tissue samples of sufficient quality. In addition, factors such as procedure duration, waiting times, resource utilization, and costs will be analyzed.
conditions: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to internal joint prosthesis

interventions.name:
Single-arm, prospective, exploratory clinical feasibility study.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a symptomatic total hip arthroplasty and suspected (low-grade) periprosthetic infection, scheduled as part of routine clinical care for diagnostic hip arthroscopy and punch biopsy according to clinical guidelines
	•	Age > 18 years
	•	Informed consent to participate in the study
Exclusion criteria:
•	Refusal to participate
	•	Lack of capacity to provide informed consent
	•	Body mass index > 45
